text_boxes.text: How can a model generate an ordered answer?
Translation, code and image transcription produce sequences.
Today: calculate attention; hide future answers; explain training versus generation.
You need short vector products, matrix shapes and probability.
Sequence generation means making ordered choices and learning when to stop.
Teaching example / proposed work — scope stated on the slide
From text to numbers: token → ID → embedding
A token may be a word, a word part, a character or a symbol.
An ID selects a learned vector; the ID itself is not a meaning score.
BOS begins a sequence; EOS ends it; PAD fills unused positions.
Lab-local token IDs; hand-chosen illustrative embeddings, not a deployed tokenizer.
Token IDs are lookup addresses; embeddings provide the model's learned input vectors.
[1] Attention Is All You Need — embeddings and softmax
A sequence is a chain of next-token decisions
p(y | x) = product over t of p(yₜ | y₍<t₎, x).
The prefix is the output already available before the next choice.
The same source x is available at every row.
Next-token probabilities combine to score a complete sequence.
Where do the next-token scores come from?
The encoder turns source input into memory vectors.
The decoder uses its prefix and can attend to source memory.
A vocabulary projection produces logits; softmax gives next-token probabilities.
S=source positions   T=prefix positions   d=hidden width   C=vocabulary size
One memory vector per source position
Causal self-attention, source cross-attention and feed-forward layers
One score per vocabulary token at each position
Use the last available position during generation
The source, the output prefix and the vocabulary distribution have different jobs.

Q asks; K is compared; V carries the information to mix.
Attention weights select how much of each whole value vector to combine.

Shapes tell us what attention is doing
Each query gets one score for every key; softmax runs over keys.
Use distinct axis sizes to expose an incorrect transpose.
The √dₖ scale helps keep scores from growing too sharp as width grows.
7 source positions; values may have a different width
5 queries × 7 keys for each batch and head
one mixed value vector per query
A score row belongs to one query; its columns are the available keys.

A causal mask blocks future input positions
Add 0 to permitted scores and −∞ to blocked scores, before softmax.
A blocked score gets attention weight 0 after softmax.
The mask is not a probability distribution; valid weight rows sum to 1.
Input I predicts love; future input position 2 is blocked.

Generation: predict → append the prediction → repeat until EOS or a length limit.

19:00–21:00 · Position information without a misleading slogan
“Dog bites person” and “Person bites dog” reuse tokens but change meaning.
Transformers commonly add or apply position information to representations.
A causal mask already has an ordered visibility pattern; removing position embeddings does not make every causal model order-blind.
Same token set, different ordered sequences. Positional vectors are one way to provide position information.
Specify both the position representation and the visibility rule when reasoning about order.

Greedy can miss the best complete sequence
Greedy chooses the best token at each step: A then X gives 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30.
Beam width 3 retains several prefixes: B then X gives 0.4 × 1.0 = 0.40.
Beam is approximate search; a higher model score does not guarantee better task accuracy.
2 symbols · beam width 3 · no length penalty
Equal-length toy; ties choose X before Y; EOS omitted here.
Decoding changes which path is selected; it does not improve the underlying probability model automatically.

Use the same ideas for an image-to-symbol project
Encode image features; generate symbols with shifted training and a causal decoder.
Compare generated outputs with held-out references and a simple baseline.
Four synthetic glyph classes demonstrate mechanics; they do not establish real OCR performance.
Source features become keys and values
Compare greedy and beam width 3 on identical cases
Compare to nearest-template baseline and inspect actual errors
A working toy system teaches mechanisms; research claims require an appropriate task and evidence.
